newsitem.title: UK: West's refinery margins rise then fall in Jan - IEA.
newsitem.headline: West's refinery margins rise then fall in Jan - IEA.

text.p: Profit margins at oil refineries in the West rose but then fell back again during January, the International Energy Agency (IEA) said on Friday.
But those in Singapore dropped so sharply that some refiners cut runs, the IEA said in its latest Monthly Oil Market Report.

Refining margins continued to be very volatile in January due to the relative sharp changes in the value of crude oil and refined oil products. While overall margins were inconsistent there was a widening spread between cracking and hydroskimming margins in all centres.

In Rotterdam and the Mediterranean, margins rose in the first two weeks of January due to a sharp rise in gas oil prices which outpaced gains on crude oil and more than offset falling heavy fuel oil prices.
But margins then fell back during the second half of the month when gas oil prices retreated and the cold weather moderated.
The downward pressure was reinforced by the continuing falls on heavy fuel, particularly on hydroskimming margins.

Average cracking margins fell slightly in Rotterdam and rose in the Mediterranean where the earlier weakening in sour crude prices relative to Brent continued to provide limited support to the region.
On the U.S. Gulf Coast, margins largely followed the pattern of gas oil prices and remained under downward pressure due to falling fuel oil prices and relatively firm crude.
Singapore margins fell sharply during January, losing almost $3 a barrel, mainly due to sharp falls in Asian gas oil and fuel oil prices.
Some refineries there cut runs during the second half of the month.

Total refinery throughputs for December in OECD countries remained at 33.8 million barrels per day (bpd), almost unchanged from November which was the highest level for more than eight years. December throughputs were nearly 600,000 bpd above year ago levels.
Rises of 150,000 bpd in Japan and 100,000 bpd in the U.S. were offset by a fall of 230,000 bpd in Europe.

Despite the fall in Europe, throughputs were still at the highest December level for more than eight years. Falls mainly due to strikes at several French refineries were partly offset by increases in Italy, Ireland and the Netherlands.

Throughputs in the U.S. rose by 100,000 bpd to 14.25 million bpd and were 240,000 bpd above year earlier levels. Firm gas oil demand and low stocks of heating oil and gasoline continued to keep throughputs at high utilisation rates.
The utilisation rate fell by just 0.5 percent from November to 95.2 percent, almost the same as the year before.
Japanese throughputs rose 150,000 bpd to almost 4.5 million bpd the highest level in nine months, consistent with the end of seasonal refinery maintenance.
In January, throughputs are thought to have risen slightly in Japan but fallen in Europe from the high levels seen in December.
Weekly U.S. data up to January 24 suggest throughputs have fallen about 560,000 bpd with the onset of the peak U.S. turnaround season.
